questions.name: Field Completeness
questions.description: Proportion of mandatory schema fields populated
questions.evidence: id: https://doi.org/10.13026/37yb-1t42, title: 'Bridge2AI-Voice - An ethically-sourced, diverse voice dataset linked to health information', description: 1000+ char comprehensive description, keywords: 71 keywords, license_and_use_terms: Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access License (detailed section at lines 865-877)
questions.quality_note: All mandatory fields present with comprehensive, high-quality content. Description is detailed and informative, keywords are extensive and specific.

questions.name: Entry Length Adequacy
questions.description: Whether narrative fields have meaningful content length
questions.evidence: description: ~1000 characters (lines 4-20), purposes: 4 entries with 150-300 chars each, tasks: 7 entries with 100-250 chars each
questions.quality_note: Narrative fields are comprehensive and exceed 200 character threshold significantly. Description provides detailed context about project goals, clinical applications, and data characteristics.

questions.name: Keyword Diversity
questions.description: Number of unique keywords provided
questions.evidence: keywords: 71 unique keywords (lines 27-76) including: voice biomarker, acoustic biomarker, Bridge2AI, voice AI, specific disorder names (Parkinson's, Alzheimer's, depression, COPD), technical terms (spectrogram, MFCC, OpenSMILE, Praat), standards (FAIR, CARE, BIDS), platforms (PhysioNet, Health Data Nexus)
questions.quality_note: Exceptional keyword diversity covering clinical domains, technical methods, ethical frameworks, and data standards. Far exceeds the ≥8 threshold with 71 well-chosen keywords.

questions.name: File Enumeration and Type Variety

questions.evidence: distribution_formats (lines 683-705): Parquet (spectrograms/features), TSV (phenotype data), JSON (data dictionaries), WAV (raw audio), GZ (compressed archives). distributions (lines 714-752): 4 distinct distribution mechanisms with format specifications

questions.name: Data File Size Availability

questions.quality_note: Excellent standardization: BIDS v1.9.0 compliance throughout, standard file formats (Parquet, TSV, JSON, WAV), explicit FAIR and CARE principles adherence, ICD-10 codes for diagnoses, PhysioNet platform compliance. Clear schema conformance and interoperability focus.

questions.name: Tool and Software Transparency

However, version numbers are not consistently provided (e.g., 'OpenAI Whisper model' without version specification, no version for OpenSMILE/Praat/Parselmouth/torchaudio/SenseLab). Score 4 due to missing version consistency, though tool documentation is otherwise excellent.

questions.name: Collection Protocol Clarity

questions.evidence: external_resources (lines 910-979): PhysioNet (https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/), Health Data Nexus (https://healthdatanexus.ai/content/b2ai-voice/1.0/), GitHub repositories (bridge2ai-docs, b2aiprep, bridge2ai-redcap), Zenodo (10.5281/zenodo.13834653), NIH RePORTER (project 3OT2OD032720-01S3), Bridge2AI program (https://bridge2ai.org), DACO (DACO@b2ai-voice.org)

Dataset ecosystem well-connected across research infrastructure.

strengths: Perfect structural completeness with all mandatory fields populated and 71 diverse keywords
Exceptional funding documentation including grant numbers, budget breakdown ($4.66M), and project timeline
Comprehensive ethical documentation: IRB approval, HIPAA Safe Harbor deidentification, Certificate of Confidentiality, informed consent procedures
Fully defined two-tier access mechanism (registered access via PhysioNet, controlled access via DACO) with clear license and DUA requirements
Excellent standardization: BIDS v1.9.0 compliance, standard file formats (Parquet, TSV, JSON, WAV, GZ), FAIR and CARE principles adherence
Outstanding collection protocol documentation: specific hardware (iPad, Avid AE-36 microphone), 22 adult + 36 pediatric tasks enumerated, compensation details
Comprehensive version history with 5 releases tracked (v1.0-v3.0.0), release dates, change summaries, and version-specific DOIs
Detailed human subjects representation: 833 adult + 300 pediatric participants, 6 clinical subpopulations with validation methods
Perfect FAIRness compliance: persistent identifiers (DOI, URLs), fully defined access paths, clear license terms, structured provenance tracking
Extensive cross-platform interlinking: PhysioNet, Health Data Nexus, GitHub (3 repos), Zenodo, NIH RePORTER, Bridge2AI program
weaknesses: Software tools documented comprehensively but missing consistent version numbers (OpenSMILE, Praat, Parselmouth, torchaudio, SenseLab versions not specified; only 'Whisper model' without version)
Limited formal peer-reviewed publication DOIs (1 conference paper at Interspeech 2024, 1 Zenodo data dictionary archive) - could benefit from additional journal publications
recommendations: Add version numbers for all software tools: OpenSMILE (e.g., 3.0), Praat (e.g., 6.3.10), Parselmouth, torchaudio, SenseLab, and specify Whisper model version (e.g., 'large-v3')
Expand associated publications section with additional peer-reviewed journal articles describing dataset methodology, validation studies, or benchmark results as they become available
Consider adding GitHub release tags or version links for b2aiprep and other open-source tools to ensure reproducibility
